Tutorial_BasicControls: Use {[RWRD:0,31,1,32]} to move your camera around. Alternatively, you can press {[RWRD:143]} and drag. Use {[RWRD:89]} to zoom in and out. To rotate hold {[RWRD:150]} and move your mouse around. Alternatively you can use {[RWRD:2]} and {[RWRD:33]}. {[RWRD:45]} will reset the camera rotation, while {[RWRD:40]} returns the camera to the Townheart. {[RWRD:47]} {[RWRD:48]} {[RWRD:62]} change the game speed. You can pause the game by pressing {[RWRD:46]}.
Tutorial_BasicControls_Joystick: You can use {[RWRD:0,31,1,32]} to look around. To zoom in and out use {[RWRD:89]}. To rotate the camera left or right use {[RWRD:2,33]}. You can use {[RWRD:40]} to re-center the camera on the Townheart. You can access different features via the menu. Press and hold {[RWRD:122]} to open the building menu. Hold {[RWRD:121]} to open various menus. Hold {[RWRD:120]} to change the gamespeed. Hold {[RWRD:123]} to change the overlays.
Tutorial_DrifterExpertise_Content_01: Drifters are skilled in certain attributes like Athletics or Cooking. These attributes determine how good they are at related tasks and how fast they can complete them.
Tutorial_DrifterExpertise_Content_02: When drifters perform tasks, they gain experience and level up. After leveling up, you can further increase their attributes in the Drifter Expertise Panel.
Tutorial_DrifterExpertise_Content_03: With each level up, a drifter gains an expertise point that you can assign to an attribute. When a drifter has unspent expertise points, navigate to the attribute you wish to improve and use {[RWRD:137]} to increase it.
Tutorial_DrifterManagement_Content_01: Your drifters will take care of any task you lay out for them. They always prioritize tasks based on their highest priority. You can adjust their priorities for various tasks such as Cooking, Salvaging, and more in the Drifter Duties Panel.
Tutorial_DrifterManagement_Content_02: To adjust how much priority your drifters give to a task, you can use {[RWRD:137]} to increase it or {[RWRD:138]} to decrease it. When the priority of multiple tasks is the same, drifters will prioritize tasks they have an affinity for. If there are still equal tasks or if the equal tasks are without an affinity, your drifters will prioritize them from left to right. To prevent drifters from doing certain tasks, simply set their priority to an empty box.
Tutorial_Energy_Content_01: In our moving town, Eel-ectricity is essential for more than just crafting or cooking - it’s what propels us forward! Suppliers, like the Townheart’s crank, generate it. Consumers, on the other hand, need it to function. Create a functional Eel-ectricity grid by linking buildings together!
Tutorial_Energy_Content_02: To link buildings, interact with their connector to attach a cable to your cursor. Then move the cable to a nearby building's connector. Once linked, these buildings will be part of the same Eel-ectricity grid.
Tutorial_Energy_Content_03_Joystick: Additionally, you can use the building’s radial menu and select one of the available links to start making a connection.
Tutorial_Energy_Content_03_Mouse: Another way to link buildings is by opening the building’s panel and using the link button in the Eel-ectricity tab.
Tutorial_InteractingLandmarks_Rescue: Surviving drifters can also be found on Landmarks. If you choose to rescue them they will join your town.
Tutorial_InteractingLandmarks_Salvage: Most landmarks have resources on them. You can task your drifters to retrieve them. To do so, you set the amount of drifters you want to send, then the preferred transportation and confirm by pressing the Salvage button.
Tutorial_InteractingLandmarks_Scouting: A few landmarks have a vantage point from which the surrounding region can be observed. You can task a drifter to scout it out, which clears the fog on the <sprite="SurvivalGuide_Sprites" sprite name="map"> map.
Tutorial_ManagingDrifters_Content_01: Drifters will follow the priorities laid out in the Drifter Duties Panel. Drifters will always do the task with the highest priority available to them. You can increase how much priority they give a task by using [LEFTMOUSE] and decrease it by using [RIGHTMOUSE]. Drifters will not do a task if their priority box is empty. (set to 0) When the priority of multiple tasks are equal, drifters will do the task they have an affinity for. After that, they will prioritize tasks from left to right.
Tutorial_ManagingDrifters_Content_01_Joy: Drifters will follow the priorities laid out in the Drifter Duties Panel. Drifters will always do the task with the highest priority available to them. You can use {[RWRD:137]} to increase how much priority they give a task, and use {[RWRD:138]} to decrease it. Drifters will not do a task if their priority box is empty. (set to 0) When the priority of multiple tasks are equal, drifters will do the task they have an affinity for. After that, they will prioritize tasks from left to right.
Tutorial_Pollution_Content_01: Drifters living in this world will obtain pollution in various ways: through eating polluted food, by salvaging polluted flotsam, cleaning polluted ingredients, and more. When a drifter becomes fully polluted, they will contract a disease.
Tutorial_Pollution_Content_02: Pollution causes various different diseases, each with its own negative effects on either the drifter or their surroundings. Your drifters will naturally recover over a few days. Alternatively, if you have a doctor, they can cure the diseased drifter by administering the correct medicine to them in the Med Pod.
Tutorial_Research_Content_01: You can unlock new technologies through research. Numerous technologies are available, each with its own Knowledge requirement.
Tutorial_Research_Content_01_B: Knowledge is obtained when drifters accumulate experience.
Tutorial_Research_Content_02: Choose a technology for your drifters to research, and they will start researching it. Keep in mind that as drifters research, the Knowledge used is consumed, so choose wisely! Multiple research stations allow you to research individual Knowledge points simultaneously.
Tutorial_SalvagingFlotsam_Content_01: Flotsam refers to resources floating in the ocean, which can be salvaged by either placing a swimming marker or a boat marker. (a boat marker requires a boat)
Tutorial_SalvagingFlotsam_Content_01_Joy: To start salvaging, target a patch of flotsam and press {[RWRD:93]}. You can then choose your preferred salvage method.
Tutorial_SalvagingFlotsam_Content_01_Mou: To salvage, open the Salvaging Panel and select the Swimming Marker. Once selected, you can choose a patch of flotsam and place it there.
Tutorial_SalvagingFlotsam_Content_02: You can increase the number of drifters that can salvage there or expand its salvaging radius by selecting the Buoy Marker.
Tutorial_TownMovement_Content_01: You can move the town across the ocean in the Map. You can use [{[RWRD:69]},{[RWRD:71]},{[RWRD:70]},{[RWRD:72]}] to move your town. Alternatively you can press and hold [LEFTMOUSE] or double-click [LEFTMOUSE] on a location to move towards it. If you prefer to switch Camera Controls with Town Movement Controls, you can do so by pressing [{[RWRD:83]}]. Moving the town costs Eel-ectricity. Drifters will use the Townheart's crank to refill it. At higher Weight tiers, it requires more energy to move.
Tutorial_TownMovement_Content_02: You can reach new destinations by moving your town across the Map.
Tutorial_TownMovement_Content_03: Additionally, you can use {[RWRD:69]}{[RWRD:71]}{[RWRD:70]}{[RWRD:72]} to move your town.
Tutorial_TownMovement_Content_04: If you prefer to switch your Camera Controls {[RWRD:79]}{[RWRD:81]}{[RWRD:80]}{[RWRD:82]} with Town Movement Controls, you can do so by pressing {[RWRD:83]}.
Tutorial_TownMovement_Content_05: You can press and hold {[RWRD:93]} on a location to move towards it.
Tutorial_TownMovement_Content_07: Moving requires Eel-ectricity. When your Eel-ectricity is low, drifters will use the Townheart's crank to refill it.
Tutorial_TownMovement_Content_08: As your town's Weight increases, the Townheart will require more Eel-ectricity to move.
Tutorial_TownMovement_Content_Joystick_0: You can use {[RWRD:69]} to accelerate and {[RWRD:71,72]} to steer your town.
Tutorial_Weight_Content_01: Each building carries a Weight. As more buildings are added, the town becomes heavier. When weight thresholds are reached, ranging from Light to Very Heavy, the cost of moving the town increases. If the maximum capacity is reached, you can't construct new buildings until you increases the weight capacity with buildings like the Town Tugger.
Tutorial_Weight_Content_01_0.9: The town has a total Weight, which is tracked in tiers. Each building adds to this weight, and when the total weight reaches a higher tier, the Eel-ectricity cost of moving the town increases.
Tutorial_Weight_Content_02_0.9: If the maximum capacity is reached, you can't construct new buildings until you increases the weight capacity with buildings like the Town Tugger.
Tutorial_Workshops_Content_01: Workshops are used by your drifters to craft resources. You can queue different recipes in each workshop, with some having multiple options. Once a recipe is queued, your drifters will begin crafting it.
Tutorial_Workshops_Content_02: Queue the desired amount using the +1 and -1 buttons. To continuously produce recipes as resources become available, use the button.

UI_Start_Information: Over the past few months we have been working to improve the speed with which we can develop new content for Flotsam. As part of this development we created several tools that allow us to build the world of Flotsam by hand. This creates a more solid foundation for crafting, testing and balancing all the new features we have lined up for future updates. This does Introduce reduced replayability, as we currently only have one hand-made world. So the choice is yours; will you play the new handcrafted world or stick with the procedurally generated world?
UI_StartingMessage:
Well that’s it then. Garbage floods wiped away our village. Perhaps we should stop sticking on these useless rocks and go explore!

Who needs land? These endless blue waves, that's all we need! The flooded world is our oyster. Let’s polish this plastic into beautiful pearls!


If only we weren't out of fuel...
